acceptance_criterion: Every status change writes a history entry containing previous status, new status, the acting user, their role, the timestamp, and the triggering action
test_name: writes the first status history entry for the submission (F1)

acceptance_criterion: An attempted transition that is not permitted from the current status is refused, and the message names the current status and the attempted target
test_name: names the current status and the attempted target when it refuses

acceptance_criterion: A venue record holds name, building/location, maximum capacity, supported room layouts with the capacity for each layout, facilities, accessibility features, and operating hours per day of week
test_name: lets Venue Staff create a venue holding every catalogue attribute

acceptance_criterion: Maximum capacity and each per-layout capacity must be whole numbers greater than zero
test_name: refuses a layout capacity of 0 or a fraction, naming the layout's row

acceptance_criterion: At least one layout must be recorded
test_name: requires at least one

acceptance_criterion: Only Venue Staff can create or update venue records; other internal roles have read access only, and an update attempt by them changes nothing
test_name: refuses an update by %s and changes nothing

acceptance_criterion: Each create or update records the acting user and the timestamp, and retains the previous values of changed fields
test_name: lets any Venue Staff member update a venue, recording only the changed fields with their previous values

acceptance_criterion: Marking a venue inactive retains its existing bookings, its history, and its visibility on the availability calendar
test_name: marks a venue inactive, keeping the record and recording the change

acceptance_criterion: A rejected update leaves every stored venue field unchanged
test_name: leaves every stored field unchanged when the update is refused

acceptance_criterion: Each notification records the recipient, the notification type, the related event reference, the creation timestamp, and a message stating what happened and to which event
test_name: records the event, its reference and the message type on every notification (T2 AC1)

acceptance_criterion: Only users with a relationship to the event receive its notifications
test_name: D4: tells the organiser of the approval

acceptance_criterion: A notification is created as part of the same operation as the triggering action; if the triggering action does not complete, no notification exists
test_name: creates one notification, and the second delivery is recognised as already handled

acceptance_criterion: The notification list shows the signed-in user's own notifications, newest first, with an unread count
test_name: lists only my own notifications, newest first, with my unread count

acceptance_criterion: A notification can be marked read individually, and all can be marked read in one action; read state is held per user
test_name: marks all of my notifications read in one action, and nobody else's

acceptance_criterion: Read state persists across sessions
test_name: marks one of my notifications read, leaving the others unread

acceptance_criterion: Opening a notification navigates to the related event when the user still has access to it
test_name: opens the related event, marking the notification read

acceptance_criterion: Notifications belonging to other users are never shown
test_name: answers 404 for someone else's notification, and leaves it unread

acceptance_criterion: The venue detail screen shows every catalogue attribute listed in H1, read from the venue catalogue
test_name: shows every catalogue attribute (H2 AC1)

acceptance_criterion: Accessibility features are listed individually rather than as a single yes/no indicator
test_name: lists each accessibility feature on its own (H2 AC2)

acceptance_criterion: Each supported layout is shown with its own capacity
test_name: shows each layout with its own capacity (H2 AC3)

acceptance_criterion: Operating hours are shown per day of week
test_name: shows opening hours for each day of the week (H2 AC4)

acceptance_criterion: Attendees cannot access the venue catalogue screens
test_name: refuses an attendee the catalogue (H2)

acceptance_criterion: Confirmation of a booking is atomic: when two approvals for overlapping periods at the same venue are processed simultaneously, exactly one results in a confirmed booking and the other is refused
test_name: N1, L3: exactly one of 50 overlapping holds on one venue succeeds; the other 49 get the conflict refusal

acceptance_criterion: Two bookings where one ends exactly when the other begins merely touch, are not treated as overlapping, and are both permitted
test_name: N1: all of 50 back-to-back holds that merely touch succeed

acceptance_criterion: The reservation is atomic with respect to the availability check: when two reservations for overlapping periods are processed simultaneously and only one unit remains, exactly one succeeds
test_name: Q1: exactly one of 50 reservations of the last free projector succeeds

acceptance_criterion: The reservation is atomic with respect to the availability check: when two reservations for overlapping periods are processed simultaneously and only one unit remains, exactly one succeeds
test_name: Q1: exactly one of 50 reservations of the last chair in bulk stock succeeds, and the rest learn they are 1 short

acceptance_criterion: The permitted statuses are exactly: Draft, Submitted, Under Review, Awaiting Clarification, Approved, Planning, Safety Review, Confirmed, Completed, Cancelled, Rejected
test_name: are exactly the eleven the story names

acceptance_criterion: Status can only be changed by an action defined in another story; there is no screen that lets a user type or pick an arbitrary status
test_name: has no statement other than updateStatusIf that sets an event's status

acceptance_criterion: An event reaches Confirmed only through the confirmation action specified in F5; this story defines that Confirmed is a permitted status and that reaching it writes a history entry like any other transition
test_name: reaches Safety Review only when F5 confirms the arrangements

acceptance_criterion: CR-06: F5's confirmation of the arrangements moves an event to Safety Review; only the Safety Officer's approval (U1) moves it to Confirmed, and a request for changes returns it to Planning; each writes a history entry
test_name: reaches Confirmed only through the Safety Officer's approval

acceptance_criterion: An event moves to Completed only after its recorded end date/time has passed
test_name: leaves an event that ends one millisecond later Confirmed
